verdicts.note: Confirmed on f98c416. If S:1691 succeeds, a zero-launch pause is written (S:1696-1697). Its resume needs 46,000+3,000=49,000 of a fixed 60,000 ms (S:1572, S:1457, S:1506): I2 must be at S:1572 within 11 s of the I1 start, impossible after a ≤30 s handshake (S:1115). The scope is wider than framed. Stale rechecks (S:1272/1276) and time refusals (S:1273/1277/1634/1636) before exit-zero also end G0. For G1-G7 a zero-launch pause is a permanent loss unless resumed within 90 s (G1/G2/G5/G6), 135 s (G3/G4) or 225 s (G7) of I1. defe073 S:1351 allowed a restart. Contradicts M:760-761.

Re-derived from M:2383, M:2703, M:811 and the command walls. Unfinished ceilings plus 3,000 before exit-one, deadline-kill, stdout-cap, stderr-cap, real-child-tree and vitest-baseline are 44,000, 39,000, 34,000, 29,000, 23,000 and 18,000 ms. A timeout of up to 30,000 ms (S:1115, clamped only to the deadline minus 3,000) leaves under 30,000 ms. The first three are therefore impossible, and the last three need all other work to take ≤1, 7 and 12 s after 4, 5 and 6 helper plus Add-Type launches. Before G0's first child it is a permanent G0 dead end (S1-01). The race window is about the length of the pre-launch IO, and it fails closed.
